title: Gluten-Free Banana Maple Cupcakes
shortDescription: Soft gluten-free banana cupcakes with maple extract frosting, ready in 25 minutes prep and 18 minutes bake.
description: These cupcakes start with really ripe, mashed bananas mixed into a gluten-free flour base. I tested this batch three times in my home kitchen to get the crumb soft, not gummy. The frosting uses maple extract instead of syrup, so it stays thick and pipes tall without going runny. You get real banana taste in every bite, plus a maple finish that never turns sticky.
ingredients: 1 1/2 cups gluten-free all purpose flour blend (with xanthan gum)
1 cup mashed ripe banana (about 2 medium bananas)
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F. Line a 12 cup muffin pan with paper liners.
Whisk the gluten-free flour, baking powder, baking soda, salt, and cinnamon in a bowl.
Beat softened butter and sugar together until light and fluffy, about 2 minutes.
Add eggs one at a time, beating well after each one.
Mix in mashed banana and vanilla extract until combined.
Add the flour mix in two batches, alternating with buttermilk. Mix just until smooth.
Divide batter evenly among liners, filling each about two thirds full.
Bake 16 to 18 minutes, until a toothpick comes out clean. Cool in the pan 5 minutes, then move to a wire rack.
For the frosting, beat softened butter until creamy. Add powdered sugar in two batches.
Mix in maple extract and heavy cream. Beat 2 minutes until light and pipeable.
Pipe frosting onto fully cooled cupcakes and serve.
tips: Use bananas with dark spotted skins. They give the strongest banana taste and natural sweetness.
Check your gluten-free flour blend has xanthan gum, or add 1/4 tsp separately for structure.
Maple extract is stronger than maple syrup, so start with 1 tsp and taste before adding more.
Let cupcakes cool completely before frosting, or the buttercream will slide off.

faq.question: Can I use maple syrup instead of maple extract in the frosting?
faq.answer: I do not recommend it here. Syrup adds liquid that thins the buttercream and can make it too soft to pipe. Maple extract gives the same flavor without changing the texture.

faq.question: Why did my gluten-free banana cupcakes turn out dense?
faq.answer: This usually means the batter was overmixed after adding the flour, or the bananas were under ripe. Mix just until combined and use bananas with brown spotted skins for best texture.

faq.question: Can I make these dairy free?
faq.answer: Yes. Swap the butter for a plant based block butter and use a dairy free milk with 1 tsp lemon juice in place of buttermilk. The crumb stays soft either way.

faq.question: How long do these cupcakes stay fresh?
faq.answer: Store them in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 4 days. Let them sit at room temperature for 20 minutes before serving so the frosting softens.

conclusion: These banana maple cupcakes prove gluten-free baking can still taste rich and homemade. The maple extract frosting holds its shape and the banana flavor stays front and center. Try them for a weekend bake or a fall bake sale, they hold up well and travel easily.
